title: One key that may log in to the FleetLedger computer (ship-fleet keys ls --json entries, version 1)
description: Each entry of `ship-fleet keys ls --json`, a list of every line with a key in the FleetLedger user's ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, then authorized_keys2, in the order sshd tries them. It only reads, and answers while the vault is locked. Never the key itself: its type and fingerprint. See contracts/ship-fleet.md.

file.description: The file in ~/.ssh it is in.

line.description: Its line number in that file.

name.description: The line's comment (what follows the key), as written: ship-fleet keys name sets it. Any text a hand edit put there; null when there is none.

type.description: The key's type as the line gives it (ssh-ed25519, ssh-rsa, ecdsa-sha2-nistp256, a security key's sk- types, ...).

fingerprint.description: As ssh-keygen -l prints it; null for a key that is not valid base64 (sshd lets nobody in with it).

access.description: What the line lets the key do. shell: log in and run anything (its options may still turn off a terminal or forwarding); command: only the command its command= option forces; bundle: a trusted machine's line in FleetLedger's block, only `ship-fleet machine-bundle <machine>` (ship-fleet untrust removes it); cert-authority: it is a CA, and any certificate it signs logs in.

machine.description: access bundle: the trusted machine; else null.

command.description: access command: the command it forces, unquoted; else null.

options.description: The line's options as written (from=, no-pty, ...); empty for none.

this_session.description: The key the ssh session running this command logged in with, as sshd says (ExposeAuthInfo); null when sshd does not say.

changeable.description: ship-fleet keys name and revoke may change this line: on FleetLedger's own VM, in authorized_keys, outside FleetLedger's block, and the block's markers intact.
